input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: Section 10 contemplates a "renewable one-year term" for Maintenance Services but the Agreement contains no renewal mechanics: there is no auto-renewal or mutual-agreement provision, no non-renewal notice window, no vendor renewal reminder, and Section 11/the Fee Schedule impose no cap on maintenance fee uplift at renewal. That leaves renewal pricing and continuity entirely undetermined and exposes us to unbounded increases. Added a renewal clause matching the preferred position (automatic 12-month renewals, 30-day customer opt-out, 60-day Garman reminder, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%), with the 60-day/5% fallback flagged in the comment.

proposal.summary: Add maintenance renewal mechanics: automatic 12-month renewals, 30-day customer opt-out, 60-day vendor renewal/price notice, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10 refers to a "renewable one-year term" but sets out no renewal mechanics or limit on maintenance fee increases, so we have added automatic twelve-month renewals that we may exit on 30 days' notice, a 60-day renewal reminder from Garman, and an uplift cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%. If a cap at that level is difficult, we can accept a 60-day non-renewal window and a 5% ceiling.

ops.text: (d) RENEWAL OF MAINTENANCE TERM. The maintenance term shall renew automatically for successive terms of twelve (12) months each, unless Sparkling gives Garman written notice of non-renewal not less than thirty (30) calendar days before the end of the then-current maintenance term. Garman shall give Sparkling written notice of the upcoming renewal, including any proposed change in maintenance fees, not less than sixty (60) calendar days before the end of the then-current maintenance term. Maintenance fees for any renewal term shall not exceed the fees payable for the then-current term increased by the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%).
